# negotiator

Buyer agent toolkit for the [Tacto Negotiation Arena](../negotiation-arena-kit/README.md): a client for every
API endpoint, a runner that plays cases (RFQ threads in parallel, Live Final waves), full telemetry, reports and
statistics, and a baseline strategy to beat.

Python 3.12 (the arena starter kit requires it); the kit is a path dependency, so the published cost function
C and the quote-PDF parsing are exactly the arena's.

## Setup

```sh
cd agent
uv sync
# the key: ARENA_API_KEY in the repo-root .env (git-ignored); ARENA_URL defaults to https://arena.tacto.ai
uv run negotiator me
```

## Commands

| Command | What |
|---|---|
| `negotiator health` / `me` | arena up, data downloads / team, practice quota, best scores |
| `negotiator cases --set practice\|sandbox\|final` · `case <id>` | case files |
| `negotiator sessions --set …` · `session <sid>` · `thread <sid> <supplier>` · `backoffice <sid>` | our sessions, state, result + trace, threads, the supplier's back office |
| `negotiator attachment <sid> <attachment_id> -o FILE` | a supplier document |
| `negotiator board` | leaderboard (for people; refused in final mode) |
| `negotiator data` | download package v1 and the Sunday release into `agent/data/` |
| `negotiator play <case_id> [--strategy tactical\|baseline]` | play one case, with telemetry and a report |
| `negotiator run --set sandbox\|practice [--cases …] [--parallel N]` | many cases in parallel (default: every hosted case of the set) |
| `negotiator final [--parallel 10]` | the Live Final: waits for each wave, plays its cases within the cap |
| `negotiator report [run_id\|latest]` · `stats` | rebuild a run's report · best/mean score per case across all runs |
| `negotiator lessons [run_id\|latest]` | per case, worst first: score, cost blocks, the supplier's reasons per round, argument checks (also written as `lessons.md` after every run) |

Global options: `--url` (e.g. a local `arena-sim`), `--key`, `--json`, `-v`.

## LLM strategy and providers

`--strategy llm` adds a model on top of the baseline: before the session opens it profiles each supplier from
its dossier (letters, notes, news, negotiation history, credit index); each round it reads the reply and picks
stance, concession, lever and arguments, and writes the e-mail text. Code still builds every term sheet from C,
inserts the checked arguments, strips IDs and figures the model wrote, and falls back to the baseline move if
the model is slow or fails.

Switch the model with one string - `--llm <provider>:<model>` or `LLM=<provider>:<model>` in `.env`:

| Spec | Protocol | Key |
|---|---|---|
| `ollama:qwen3.6:latest` (default) | OpenAI-compatible, `http://localhost:11434/v1`, thinking off | – |
| `openai:<model>` | OpenAI | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `openrouter:<vendor>/<model>` | OpenAI-compatible | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| `groq:` · `mistral:` · `deepseek:` · `together:` | OpenAI-compatible | `<PROVIDER>_API_KEY` |
| `compat:<model>` | any OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `LLM_BASE_URL` | `LLM_API_KEY` |
| `anthropic:<model>` | Anthropic messages | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |

Tuning: `LLM_REASONING` (`none|low|medium|high`, sent as `reasoning_effort`), `LLM_TIMEOUT_S` (default 30: each
e-mail must reach the arena within 60 s of the reply), `LLM_PARALLEL` (concurrent calls, default 4).

```sh
uv run negotiator run --set sandbox --strategy llm
uv run negotiator play case:P05 --strategy llm --llm anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5
```

## Telemetry: `runs/<run_id>/`

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `events.jsonl` | every event: `session_opened` (opening C per supplier), `plan`, `message_sent` (sheets with C), `reply` (status, terms, C, claim results, signals, latency), `attachment`, `thread_hold`, `decision`, `conflict`, `result` |
| `http.jsonl` | every HTTP attempt: endpoint, status, latency, retry, move id, pacing wait, practice quota left |
| `run.log` | the human-readable log (debug level) |
| `sessions/<sid>.json` | the whole case: case file, e-mails both ways, documents as text, decisions with rationale, result, the arena's trace and back office |
| `sessions/<sid>/` | the documents suppliers attached (quote PDF, cost breakdown XLSX, …) |
| `metrics.json` | counters (HTTP status, claim results, supplier statuses, timeouts, deals, LLM calls, errors, tokens, fallbacks) and timings (supplier reply, decision delay after a reply, HTTP latency per endpoint, LLM latency per purpose, case duration) |
| `events.jsonl` → `llm_call`, `profile` | ev

... [1476 characters truncated] ...

/ conclude /
keepalive` (see `strategy/base.py`) and register it in `strategy/__init__.py`.

**Tactical (default):** the category goal sets the policy (anchor depth, Boulware beta, reciprocity, which
levers to trade); the supplier's profile adjusts it. Concessions are counted in C: Boulware over the rounds the
round limit and the clock leave, capped tit-for-tat by the supplier's last move (no move from it, no move from us;
a half step after two stalls; the third settles the thread). Each round sends up to three sheets of equal C: our
C-optimal terms, a trade the supplier values (early payment for the cash-short, a long commitment for those who want
volume), a pure price move. Arguments are chosen by profile; irrelevant or contradicted kinds are dropped. A final
offer is probed once only when walking would cost little. The guards (`guards.py`) refuse any accept that breaks a
must-have (read on the quote PDF's standard terms; unknown counts as broken) or loses to the alternative. The tactics
are inspired by ASTRA (Kwon et al., [DSincerity/ASTRA-NegoAgent](https://github.com/DSincerity/ASTRA-NegoAgent)):
opponent modelling, an optimiser over the cost function, offers of equal value, tit-for-tat - no code taken.

**Baseline:** a target price from the lower of opening and current price minus an anchor per category goal
(floored at should-cost, plus the sustainable margin where squeezing the supplier costs C); up to three
checkable arguments (short notice vs. contract, index moves below the asked increase, weak scorecard,
should-cost, alternative quote, a cheaper rival in an RFQ); a concession schedule; three term sheets per round
(C-optimal terms, a pure price move on the supplier's terms, a shorter-payment variant at equal C); it holds a
thread on agreed / final offer / stall / close enough / last round and accepts the cheapest standing sheet that
beats the alternative.

## Tests

```sh
uv run pytest        # unit tests + end to end against a local arena-sim (started by the tests)
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
```

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
| Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the

## Conclusions

1. **The mechanics drove the gain, not the LLM.** The equal-C menu and reciprocal concessions lifted baseline on the
   arena from 0.346 to 0.736. Tactical is built on the same ideas and is also far above the old baseline.
2. **The results are noisy.** One run per case, and the bots answer non-deterministically, so the gap between
   baseline v2 (0.736) and tactical (0.639) is not reliable. It needs repeated runs.
3. **Tactical probably trails on D02 because of its shallow anchor.** Its anchor is at most −15 % below the quote,
   while the supplier's floor there is about −24 % below the opening.
4. **The LLM layer does not pay off yet.** On v2 it is worse than plain baseline: the model concedes more cautiously
   than these bots require. The natural place for a model is choosing the aggressiveness (jev), not replacing the logic.
5. **The test base is narrow.** Everything was measured on two demo cases. The real practice cases with supplier data
   (P01–P19) are untested.

## What we learned about the supplier bots (trace and back office)

- **Term structure can matter more than price.** In D01 the best deal is a 24-month contract, 60 days' payment and a
  price valid from April, at about €50.13 per unit. With a 12-month contract the second year of the horizon is bought at
  the fallback price: roughly €30k more at almost the same unit price.
- **A supplier's floor can be far below its opening.** In D02 the best deal is about €13.0 per unit against openings of
  16.0 and 17.1 (−19 to −24 %). An early `agreed` to our offer means we overpaid.
- **The bots name their levers.** Examples: "Faster payment is welcome; we can reflect it in the price", "A binding
  higher volume would help".
- **Citing a cheaper rival works.** Example: "I give half the step now and check the rest".
- **Persistence breaks the approval ladder.** "wants more than my band allows" → the owner approves the next step.
- **Unbacked claims hurt.** Benchmarks, volumes or competitors without an ID trigger "Which figures is that based on?
  Please send us the data.", and trust drops.
- **Inconsistency is punished.** When the price of the same option dropped against the previous e-mail, the supplier
  answered with a `final_offer`.

332	                    self.used_rival_refs.update((sid, r) for r in e.refs)
333	                else:
334	                    self.used_refs.update(e.refs)
335	            return picked

337	    def _rival_evidence(self, neg: Negotiation, sid: str) -> Evidence | None:
338	        """In an RFQ: a rival's standing offer that is cheaper than this supplier's."""
339	        if len(neg.threads) < 2:
340	            return None
341	        mine = neg.threads[sid].standing[1].get("unit_price")
342	        best = None
343	        for other, t in neg.threads.items():
344	            offer_id, terms = t.standing
345	            if other == sid or not offer_id or terms.get("unit_price") is None:
346	                continue
347	            if mine and terms["unit_price"] < mine and (best is None or terms["unit_price"] < best[1]):
348	                best = (offer_id, terms["unit_price"])
349	        if not best:
350	            return None
351	        return Evidence(
352	            kind="rival_offer",
353	            refs=[best[0]],
354	            sentence=f"Another bidder offers EUR {best[1]:.2f} per unit ({best[0]}).",
355	            strength=3.0,
356	        )

358	    def _message(
359	        self, neg: Negotiation, plan: SupplierPlan, sheets: list[dict], claims: list[Evidence], first: bool
360	    ) -> dict:
361	        case = neg.case
362	        lines = [f"Dear {plan.name} team," if plan.name != plan.supplier_id else "Dear Sir or Madam,", ""]
363	        if first:
364	            lines.append(
365	                "thank you for your quote. We have reviewed it against our data and cannot accept it as it stands."
366	            )
367	        else:
368	            lines.append("thank you for your reply. We have moved towards you; we need you to move as well.")
369	        lines += [c.sentence for c in claims]
370	        if first and not plan.asked_cost_breakdown:
371	            lines.append("Could you send us a cost breakdown for this part?")
372	            plan.asked_cost_breakdown = True
373	        lines.append("")
374	        lines.append("We can award on any of these options:" if len(sheets) > 1 else "Our proposal:")
375	        for i, sheet in enumerate(sheets):
376	            lines.append(f"Option {chr(65 + i)}: {describe(case, sheet['terms'])}")
377	        lines += ["", SIGNATURE]
378	        refs = sorted({r for c in claims for r in c.refs})
379	        return {
380	            "subject": f"{case.get('title', 'Your quote')}",
381	            "body": "\n".join(lines),
382	            "term_sheets": sheets,
383	            "refs": refs,
384	        }

386	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ closing
387	    def conclude(self, neg: Negotiation) -> Decision:
388	        c_alt = neg.c_alt
389	        best = None
390	        for sid, t in neg.threads.items():
391	            sheet_id, terms = t.standing
392	            if not sheet_id or t.closed or t.status in ("walked_away", "no_bid"):
393	                continue
394	            if not neg.keeps_must_haves(sid, terms):
395	                continue
396	            c = neg.cost(sid, terms)
397	            if best is None or c < best[0]:
398	                best = (c, sid, sheet_id)
399	        if best and best[0] < c_alt:
400	            return Decision(
401	                "accept",
402	                best[1],
403	                term_sheet_id=best[2],
404	                rationale={
405	                    "c": best[0],
406	                    "c_alt": c_alt,
407	                    "why": "cheapest standing sheet beats the alternative",
408	                },
409	            )
410	        return Decision(
411	            "walk_away",
412	            next(iter(neg.threads)),
413	            rationale={
414	                "c_best_standing": best[0] if best else None,
415	                "c_alt": c_alt,
416	                "why": "nothing beats the alternative",
417	            },
418	        )
419	
420	    def keepalive(self, neg: Negotiation, supplier_id: str) -> dict | None:
421	        t = neg.threads[supplier_id]
422	        if neg.case.get("round_limit", 10) - t.rounds_used <= 2:
423	            return None
424	        return {
425	            "subject": f"{neg.case.get('title', 'Your quote')}",
426	            "body": f"Dear {self.plans[supplier_id].name} team,\n\nthank you. While we complete our evaluation: "
427	            f"could you confirm your delivery capacity for our annual volume?\n\n{SIGNATURE}",
428	        }

432	    """The non-price terms of a sheet: offers with the same structure must never get cheaper."""
433	    return repr(sorted((k, v) for k, v in terms.items() if k != "unit_price"))

436	def describe(case: dict, terms: dict) -> str:
437	    """A term sheet in words, for the e-mail body (the term sheet itself is what binds)."""
438	    unit = (case.get("buyer") or {}).get("price_unit")
439	    parts = []
440	    for k, v in terms.items():
441	        if k == "unit_price":
442	            parts.append(f"EUR {v:,.2f} per unit" + (f" ({unit})" if unit else ""))
443	        elif k == "payment_days":
444	            parts.append(f"payment {v} days net")
445	        elif k == "lead_time_days":
446	            parts.append(f"lead time {v} days")
447	        elif k == "contract_months":
448	            parts.append(f"{v}-month contract" if v else "single order")
449	        elif k == "volume_per_year":
450	            parts.append(f"{v:,} units a year")
451	        elif k == "effective_date":
452	            parts.append(f"price valid from {v}")
453	        elif k == "index_clause":
454	            parts.append(
455	                "no index clause"
456	                if not v
457	                else f"index clause on {v['series']} ({v['material_share']:.0%} material, deadband "
458	                f"{v['deadband_pct']}%, base {v['base_month']})"
459	            )
460	        elif k == "incoterm":
461	            parts.append(f"Incoterm {v}")
462	        elif k == "tooling_eur":
463	            parts.append(f"tooling EUR {v:,.2f}")
464	        elif k == "ppm_commitment":
465	            parts.append(f"quality commitment {v} ppm")
466	        elif k == "chargeback_eur_per_complaint":
467	            parts.append(f"chargeback EUR {v} per complaint")
468	        else:
469	            parts.append(f"{k} {v}")
470	    return ", ".join(parts)

95	class Negotiation:
96	    def __init__(
97	        self,
98	        client: ArenaClient,
99	        recorder: Recorder,
100	        data: WorldData | None = None,
101	        *,
102	        deadline: float | None = None,
103	        strategy_name: str = "",
104	    ) -> None:
105	        self.client, self.recorder, self.data = client, recorder, data
106	        self.deadline = deadline  # wall clock (time.time()) by which the case must close, e.g. a wave cap
107	        self.strategy_name = strategy_name
108	        self.case: dict = {}
109	        self.case_id = ""
110	        self.session_id = ""
111	        self.threads: dict[str, ThreadState] = {}
112	        self.decisions: list[dict] = []
113	        self.result: dict | None = None
114	        self.ended = threading.Event()

119	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ open / resume
120	    def open(self, case_id: str, case: dict | None = None) -> "Negotiation":
121	        self.case_id = case_id
122	        try:
123	            reply = self.client.open_session(case_id)
124	        except ArenaError as e:
125	            running = _running_session(e)
126	            if not running:
127	                raise
128	            return self.resume(running, case)
129	        self.session_id, self.case = reply["session_id"], reply["case"]
130	        if self.data:
131	            self.data.with_case(self.case)
132	        for sid, messages in reply["threads"].items():
133	            state = ThreadState(sid)
134	            for message in messages:
135	                state.messages.append(self._with_documents(message, sid))
136	            self.threads[sid] = state
137	        self._log_open(resumed=False)
138	        return self

140	    def resume(self, session_id: str, case: dict | None = None) -> "Negotiation":
141	        """Pick up a session this team already started (after a crash, or a final 409)."""
142	        self.session_id = session_id
143	        state = self.client.session(session_id)
144	        self.case_id = state.get("case_id", self.case_id)
145	        self.case = case or self.case
146	        for sid in state.get("threads", {}):
147	            thread = self.client.thread(session_id, sid)
148	            ts = ThreadState(sid, closed=thread.get("closed"))
149	            ts.messages = [
150	                self._with_documents(m, sid) if m.get("from") != "buyer" else m for m in thread.get("messages", [])
151	            ]
152	            self.threads[sid] = ts
153	        if state.get("status") == "ended":
154	            self.result = state.get("result") or {"deal": False, "end_reason": state.get("end_reason")}
155	            self.ended.set()
156	        self._log_open(resumed=True)
157	        return self

162	            sheet_id, terms = t.standing
163	            opening[sid] = {

175	            suppliers=list(self.threads),
176	            resumed=resumed,
177	            opening=opening,

190	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ documents
191	    def _with_documents(self, message: dict, supplier_id: str) -> dict:
192	        """Download every attachment of a supplier message, save the file, add its text."""
193	        for att in message.get("attachments") or []:
194	            if not att.get("attachment_id") or "text" in att:
195	                continue
196	            try:
197	                blob = self.client.attachment(self.session_id, att["attachment_id"])
198	            except ArenaError as e:
199	                log.warning("attachment %s: %s", att["attachment_id"], e)
200	                continue
201	            path = self.recorder.session_dir(self.session_id) / safe_name(f"{supplier_id}-{att['name']}")
202	            path.write_bytes(blob)
203	            try:
204	                att["text"] = read_document(att["name"], blob)
205	            except Exception as e:  # a document we cannot parse must not stop the case
206	                att["text"] = ""
207	                log.warning("cannot read %s: %s", att["name"], e)
208	            att["file"] = str(path.relative_to(self.recorder.dir))
209	            self.recorder.metrics.incr(f"documents.{att.get('type', 'unknown')}")
210	            self.recorder.event(
211	                "attachment",
212	                session_id=self.session_id,
213	                supplier_id=supplier_id,
214	                name=att["name"],
215	                type=att.get("type"),
216	                bytes=len(blob),
217	                file=att["file"],
218	            )
219	        return message

232	    @property
233	    def c_open(self) -> float:
234	        """Our estimate of C_open: the cheapest opening quote that keeps the must-haves."""
235	        best = math.inf
236	        for sid, t in self.threads.items():
237	            first = next((m for m in t.supplier_messages if m.get("term_sheets")), None)
238	            if first and self.keeps_must_haves(sid, first["term_sheets"][0]["terms"]):
239	                best = min(best, self.cost(sid, first["term_sheets"][0]["terms"]))

242	    def cost(self, supplier_id: str, terms: dict) -> float:
243	        if not terms or terms.get("unit_price") is None:
244	            return math.inf
245	        t = self.threads.get(supplier_id)
246	        return total_cost(self.case, terms, t.standard_terms if t else None, self.supplier_estimates.get(supplier_id))

252	            for k, v in cost_breakdown(
253	                self.case, terms, t.standard_terms if t else None, self.supplier_estimates.get(supplier_id)
254	            ).items()

264	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ moves
265	    def send(self, supplier_id: str, message: dict, rationale: dict | None = None) -> dict | None:
266	        """Send one e-mail; returns the supplier's reply (None if the case ended meanwhile)."""
267	        t = self.threads[supplier_id]
268	        message, removed = clean_message(self, supplier_id, message)
269	        if removed:
270	            self.recorder.metrics.incr("guards.removed", len(removed))
271	            self.recorder.event("guard_cleaned", session_id=self.session_id, supplier_id=supplier_id, removed=removed)
272	            log.warning("%s: guard removed %s", supplier_id, removed)
273	        waited = t.seconds_since_reply()
274	        if waited > MOVE_LIMIT_S * 0.8:
275	            log.warning("%s: answering %.0fs after its reply (limit %.0fs)", supplier_id, waited, MOVE_LIMIT_S)
276	        self.recorder.metrics.observe("decision.seconds_after_reply", waited)
277	        sheets = [
278	            {"terms": s["terms"], "c": self.cost(supplier_id, s["terms"])} for s in message.get("term_sheets", [])
279	        ]
280	        round_no = t.rounds_used + 1
281	        self._decision("message", supplier_id, rationale, round=round_no, sheets=sheets)
282	        self.recorder.event(
283	            "message_sent",
284	            session_id=self.session_id,
285	            case_id=self.case_id,
286	            supplier_id=supplier_id,
287	            round=round_no,
288	            subject=message.get("subject"),
289	            body=message.get("body"),
290	            term_sheets=sheets,
291	            refs=message.get("refs", []),
292	            seconds_after_reply=round(waited, 2),
293	        )
294	        start = time.perf_counter()
295	        try:
296	            reply = self.client.send_message(self.session_id, supplier_id, message)
297	        except ArenaError as e:
298	            if e.status == 422:
299	                self.recorder.metrics.incr("moves.invalid")
300	                self.recorder.event(
301	                    "invalid_move", session_id=self.session_id, supplier_id=supplier_id, detail=e.detail
302	                )
303	                log.error("%s: invalid message: %s", supplier_id, e.detail)
304	                raise
305	            if e.status != 409:
306	                raise
307	            self.recorder.metrics.incr("moves.conflict")
308	            self._refresh_after_conflict(supplier_id, e)
309	            return None if self.ended.is_set() else t.latest
310	        took = time.perf_counter() - start
311	        self.recorder.metrics.observe("supplier.reply_seconds", took)
312	        with t.lock:
313	            t.messages.append({**message, "from": "buyer", "sent_at": utc_now()})
314	            t.messages.append(self._with_documents(reply, supplier_id))
315	            t.last_reply_at = time.monotonic()
316	        self._log_reply(supplier_id, reply, took, round_no)
317	        if reply.get("status") in ENDED_STATUSES:
318	            t.closed = reply["status"]
319	        return reply

360	        """After a 409: late (timeout), round limit, or the thread/case ended - read the arena's state."""
361	        self.recorder.event("conflict", session_id=self.session_id, supplier_id=supplier_id, detail=error.detail)

369	        t = self.threads[supplier_id]

371	            t.messages = [
372	                self._with_documents(m, supplier_id) if m.get("from") != "buyer" else m

374	            ]
375	            t.timeouts = len(thread.get("timeouts") or [])
376	            t.closed = thread.get("closed")
377	            t.last_reply_at = time.monotonic()

382	        if problems := accept_problems(self, supplier_id, term_sheet_id):
383	            self.recorder.metrics.incr("guards.accept_refused")
384	            self.recorder.event("guard_refused", session_id=self.session_id, supplier_id=supplier_id, problems=problems)
385	            raise GuardRefused(f"{supplier_id} {term_sheet_id}: {'; '.join(problems)}")
386	        terms = self.threads[supplier_id].standing[1]
387	        self._decision(
388	            "accept",
389	            supplier_id,
390	            rationale,

"""Hard rules that keep a case from scoring 0 by mistake. Code, not judgement; checked before every
send and every accept, whatever the strategy decided.

Accept:  the sheet is the supplier's current standing offer; it keeps every must-have on the terms
         it would really close on (sheet, then the supplier's standard terms from its quote PDF) -
         and a must-have field we cannot read from either counts as broken; C is finite and beats
         the alternative - and, when there is one, the cheapest opening too (else the alternative
         scores at least as much).
Send:    every term sheet carries exactly the negotiable fields with allowed values and keeps the
         must-haves (a supplier may agree to any sheet we send, and we must be able to accept it);
         every cited ID exists in the data, the case's facts or this session's offers; at most 3
         sheets and 20 refs.
"""

import math
import re

from arena_kit.cost import must_haves_ok

ID_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?:idx|quote|offer|sc|qn|po|cost|fc|news|doc|ctr):[\w.:@#/-]*\w")
MAX_SHEETS = 3
MAX_REFS = 20


def unreadable_must_have_fields(case: dict, terms: dict, standard: dict | None) -> list[str]:
    """Must-have fields neither the sheet, the supplier's standard terms nor the case fixes.

    `closing_terms` fills such gaps from the buyer's plan (e.g. lead time = what we need), which
    would let a sheet pass that the arena closes on the supplier's real standard - unknown to us."""
    known = {**(standard or {}), **case.get("fixed_terms", {}), **{k: v for k, v in terms.items() if v is not None}}
    return [m["field"] for m in case["buyer"].get("must_haves", []) if m["field"] not in known]


def accept_problems(neg, supplier_id: str, term_sheet_id: str | None) -> list[str]:
    """Why accepting this sheet would be a mistake (empty: safe)."""
    t = neg.threads.get(supplier_id)
    if t is None:
        return ["unknown supplier"]
    standing_id, terms = t.standing
    problems = []
    if not term_sheet_id or term_sheet_id != standing_id:
        problems.append(f"{term_sheet_id} is not the standing offer {standing_id}")
    if not terms or terms.get("unit_price") is None:
        problems.append("the standing offer has no price")
        return problems
    std = t.standard_terms
    if missing := unreadable_must_have_fields(neg.case, terms, std):
        problems.append(f"must-have field(s) {missing} unknown: no quote PDF standard terms")
    if not must_haves_ok(neg.case, terms, std):
        problems.append("breaks a must-have")
    c = neg.cost(supplier_id, terms)
    if not math.isfinite(c):
        problems.append("C is not finite")
    elif c >= neg.c_alt:
        problems.append(f"C {c:,.0f} does not beat the alternative {neg.c_alt:,.0f}")
    elif math.isfinite(neg.c_alt) and c >= neg.c_open:
        # a deal no better than the cheapest opening scores 0; the alternative scores at least that
        problems.append(f"C {c:,.0f} is not better than the opening {neg.c_open:,.0f}")
    return problems


def sheet_problems(case: dict, terms: dict) -> list[str]:
    problems = []
    negotiable = case["negotiable"]
    if set(terms) != set(negotiable):
        problems.append(f"fields {sorted(terms)} != negotiable {sorted(negotiable)}")
    options = case.get("term_options", {})
    for f, v in terms.items():
        if f == "unit_price":
            if not isinstance(v, int | float) or v <= 0:
                problems.append(f"unit_price {v!r}")
        elif options.get(f) and v not in options[f]:
            problems.append(f"{f}={v!r} not in options")
    if not must_haves_ok(case, terms):
        problems.append("breaks a must-have")
    return problems


def known_id(neg, ref: str) -> bool:
    if neg.data and neg.data.fact(ref):
        return True
    if ref in (neg.case.get("facts") or {}):
        return True
    return any(
        s.get("term_sheet_id") == ref
        for t in neg.threads.values()
        for m in t.supplier_messages
        for s in m.get("term_sheets") or []
    )


def clean_message(neg, supplier_id: str, message: dict) -> tuple[dict, list[str]]:
    """The message with invalid sheets and unknown IDs removed, and what was removed."""
    removed: list[str] = []
    sheets = []
    for sheet in (message.get("term_sheets") or [])[:MAX_SHEETS]:
        problems = sheet_problems(neg.case, sheet.get("terms", {}))
        if problems:
            removed.append(f"sheet {sheet.get('terms')}: {'; '.join(problems)}")
        elif sheet not in sheets:
            sheets.append(sheet)
    refs = []
    for ref in message.get("refs") or []:
        if known_id(neg, ref):
            if ref not in refs:
                refs.append(ref)
        else:
            removed.append(f"ref {ref}")

    def keep(m: re.Match) -> str:
        if known_id(neg, m.group(0)):
            return m.group(0)
        removed.append(f"body id {m.group(0)}")
        return ""

    body = ID_RE.sub(keep, message.get("body") or "")
    body = re.sub(r"\s*\(\s*[,;\s]*\)", "", body)
    out = {**message, "body": body[:8000], "subject": (message.get("subject") or "")[:300], "refs": refs[:MAX_REFS]}
    if "term_sheets" in message:
        out["term_sheets"] = sheets
    return out, removed
"""Ground truth before the first move: where the supplier cannot go below, and what we accept at most.

  lower bound  the supplier's floor price: its full cost (should-cost of its own plant, moved with the
               part's cost drivers since the estimate, scaled by country), a little under it when it has
               sold below cost before; without a should-cost, the price history minus a wide margin.
  upper bound  the most we accept if the deal is at risk - never said, never offered: the price the
               market justifies (cost drivers x index moves) or what this supplier usually settles at
               (asked minus its typical give), whichever is lower; never below the lower bound, never
               above its quote.

Both are prices per the case's price unit; the strategy turns them into C with the cost function.
Pure SQL and arithmetic: milliseconds, so it runs after the session opened without touching the clock.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from negotiator.data import WorldData

# full cost relative to a German cost base (company.md, should-cost rule of thumb)
COUNTRY_FACTOR = {"DE": 1.0, "AT": 1.05, "CH": 1.05, "CZ": 0.82, "PL": 0.82, "HU": 0.82, "TR": 0.75, "CN": 0.7}
BELOW_COST_FLOOR = 0.95  # a supplier that sold below full cost may do so again, not by much
NO_COST_FLOOR = 0.90  # without a should-cost: at most 10 % under the lower of its quote and our price
DEFAULT_GIVE_PCT = 2.5  # renewals settled 2.5 points under the ask on average (negotiation_history)


@dataclass
class Driver:
    series: str
    weight: float
    change_pct: float
    refs: list[str]


@dataclass
class GroundTruth:
    supplier_id: str
    part_id: str | None
    current_price: float | None
    open_price: float | None
    full_cost: float | None = None
    full_cost_source: str = ""
    lower: float | None = None
    upper: float | None = None
    asked_pct: float | None = None
    justified_pct: float | None = None  # what the cost drivers support over the last 12 months
    give_pct: float = DEFAULT_GIVE_PCT
    drivers: list[Driver] = field(default_factory=list)
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def market_supports_ask(self) -> bool:
        """The indices back the supplier: arguing them would hurt us."""
        return (
            self.asked_pct is not None and self.justified_pct is not None and self.justified_pct >= self.asked_pct - 0.5
        )

    def summary(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "part": self.part_id,
            "current": self.current_price,
            "open": self.open_price,
            "full_cost": self.full_cost,
            "full_cost_source": self.full_cost_source,
            "lower": self.lower,
            "upper": self.upper,
            "asked_pct": self.asked_pct,
            "justified_pct": self.justified_pct,
            "give_pct": self.give_pct,
            "market_supports_ask": self.market_supports_ask,
            "notes": self.notes,
        }


def justified_change(data: WorldData, part_id: str, months: int = 12) -> tuple[float | None, list[Driver]]:
    """Sum over the part's cost drivers of weight x index change over the last `months` (the share
    no driver covers is taken as flat). The IDs make each driver a checkable argument."""
    drivers = []
    total, found = 0.0, False
    for d in data.query("SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = ?", (part_id,)):
        change = data.index_change(d["series_id"], months)
        if not change or not d["weight"]:
            continue
        earlier, later, pct = change
        drivers.append(Driver(d["series_id"], d["weight"], round(pct, 2), [earlier, later]))
        total += d["weight"] * pct
        found = True
    return (round(total, 2) if found else None), drivers


def _cost_drift(data: WorldData, part_id: str, since_month: str) -> float:
    """How the part's cost moved since the should-cost estimate, by its cost drivers (fraction)."""
    total = 0.0
    for d in data.query("SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = ?", (part_id,)):
        rows = data.query(
            "SELECT month, value FROM index_values WHERE series_id = ? AND month >= ? ORDER BY month",
            (d["series_id"], since_month),
        )
        if len(rows) >= 2 and rows[0]["value"]:
            total += (d["weight"] or 0) * (rows[-1]["value"] / rows[0]["value"] - 1)
    return total


def full_cost(data: WorldData, part_id: str, supplier_id: str) -> tuple[float | None, str]:
    """The supplier's full cost per unit now: its own plant's should-cost, else the German estimate
    scaled by its country; moved with the cost drivers since the estimate."""
    rows = data.query(
        "SELECT unit_cost, supplier_id, estimate_date FROM should_cost WHERE part_id = ? ORDER BY estimate_date DESC",
        (part_id,),
    )
    if not rows:
        return None, ""
    own = [r for r in rows if r["supplier_id"] == supplier_id]
    if own:
        row, factor, source = own[0], 1.0, "own plant"
    else:
        generic = [r for r in rows if not r["supplier_id"]]
        if not generic:
            return None, ""  # another supplier's plant says little about this one
        country = (data.supplier(supplier_id).get("country") or "DE").upper()
        row, factor, source = generic[0], COUNTRY_FACTOR.get(country, 1.0), f"DE base x {country}"
    drift = _cost_drift(data, part_id, (row["estimate_date"] or "")[:7]) if row["estimate_date"] else 0.0
    return round(row["unit_cost"] * factor * (1 + drift), 2), source


def last_price(data: WorldData, part_id: str, supplier_id: str) -> float | None:
    rows = data.query(
        "SELECT price FROM price_conditions WHERE part_id = ? AND supplier_id = ? ORDER BY valid_from DESC LIMIT 1",
        (part_id, supplier_id),
    )
    return rows[0]["price"] if rows else None


def estimate(data: WorldData | None, case: dict, supplier_id: str, open_price: float | None, traits=()) -> GroundTruth:
    parts = case.get("parts") or []
    part = parts[0] if len(parts) == 1 else None  # a kit's price is not one part's cost
    buyer = case.get("buyer", {})
    current = buyer.get("current_unit_price")
    gt = GroundTruth(supplier_id, part, current, open_price)
    if open_price is None:
        gt.notes.append("no quoted price")
        return gt
    if data and part:
        current = current or last_price(data, part, supplier_id)
        gt.current_price = current
        gt.full_cost, gt.full_cost_source = full_cost(data, part, supplier_id)
        gt.justified_pct, gt.drivers = justified_change(data, part)
    if data:
        gives = data.query(
            "SELECT asked_pct - settled_pct AS give FROM negotiation_history WHERE supplier_id = ? "
            "AND asked_pct IS NOT NULL AND settled_pct IS NOT NULL",
            (supplier_id,),
        )
        if gives:
            gt.give_pct = round(sum(g["give"] for g in gives) / len(gives), 2)
    trigger = (data.fact(case["trigger_doc"]) if data and case.get("trigger_doc") else None) or {}
    if trigger.get("supplier") == supplier_id and trigger.get("asked_pct") is not None:
        gt.asked_pct = trigger["asked_pct"]
    elif current and open_price > current:
        gt.asked_pct = round((open_price / current - 1) * 100, 2)

    # lower bound: the supplier's floor
    base = min(open_price, current) if current else open_price
    if gt.full_cost:
        floor = gt.full_cost * (
            BELOW_COST_FLOOR if "below_cost" in traits or (current and current < gt.full_cost) else 1.0
        )
        gt.notes.append(f"full cost {gt.full_cost} ({gt.full_cost_source})")
    else:
        floor = base * NO_COST_FLOOR
        gt.notes.append("no should-cost: floor from prices")
    gt.lower = round(min(floor, open_price), 2)

    # upper bound: the most we accept when the deal is at risk
    candidates = [open_price * (1 - gt.give_pct / 100)]  # where it usually ends
    if current and gt.asked_pct is not None:
        candidates.append(current * (1 + (gt.asked_pct - gt.give_pct) / 100))
        if gt.justified_pct is not None:
            candidates.append(current * (1 + max(gt.justified_pct, 0.0) / 100))  # what the market supports
    upper = min(candidates)
    gt.upper = round(min(max(upper, gt.lower), open_price), 2)
    return gt

"""Single-tactic experiments on top of the baseline: each variant changes one thing, so a benchmark run
shows what that tactic alone is worth against the supplier bots (results: docs/BENCHMARKS.md).

  lowball    a deeper opening anchor: ask for less than we need, so the middle lands in our favour
  questions  three questions in every e-mail: make answering us more work than agreeing
  polite     a warm, appreciative tone
  shelby     a curt, hard tone with a threat to place the order elsewhere
  budget     a ceiling set by a third party ("management released at most EUR X") that we do not cross
  trade      no price move without a move from the supplier, and said so: every option is a trade

Everything else - term sheets from C, arguments, holding and closing - is the baseline's.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass

from negotiator.session import Negotiation
from negotiator.strategy.baseline import GOAL_ANCHOR, BaselineStrategy, SupplierPlan
from negotiator.telemetry import log

# tone -> (first e-mail, later e-mails, closing line or None)
TONES = {
    "polite": (
        "thank you very much for your quote and for the good cooperation - we appreciate the work your team puts "
        "into it. We would like to find a solution that works for both sides; as it stands the quote is above what "
        "we can accept.",
        "thank you for your reply and for moving towards us - we appreciate it. We have moved as well and hope you "
        "can take a further step.",
        "Thank you for your support - we are confident we will find an agreement.",
    ),
    "shelby": (
        "we have read your quote. It is not a number we will sign.",
        "you have moved a little. It is not enough. We have moved too, and we do not move twice for nothing.",
        "This order will be placed either way - with you or without you. Your move.",
    ),
}
QUESTIONS = [
    "What lead time can you commit to for the first call-off?",
    "Which share of your price is material, and which index does it follow?",
    "How much free capacity do you have for this part in the coming quarter?",
    "Who on your side has to approve a price below your quote?",
    "Would faster payment or a longer commitment help you more?",
    "What defect rate do you achieve on comparable parts?",
    "What would a higher annual volume change in your calculation?",
    "Which Incoterm and packaging are cheapest for you?",
    "Can you hold the price for the whole term without an index clause?",
]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tactic:
    name: str
    anchor_scale: float = 1.0  # multiplies the baseline's anchor per category goal
    tone: str | None = None  # a key of TONES; None: the baseline's wording
    questions_per_round: int = 0
    budget_share: float | None = None  # ceiling = target + share x (opening - target); None: no ceiling
    conditional: bool = False  # the supplier does not move -> we do not move at all


TACTICS = {
    t.name: t
    for t in (
        Tactic("lowball", anchor_scale=1.5),
        Tactic("questions", questions_per_round=3),
        Tactic("polite", tone="polite"),
        Tactic("shelby", tone="shelby"),
        Tactic("budget", budget_share=0.5),
        Tactic("trade", conditional=True),
    )
}


class ExperimentStrategy(BaselineStrategy):
    def __init__(self, tactic: Tactic, data=None, llm=None) -> None:
        super().__init__(data, llm)
        self.tactic = tactic
        self.name = tactic.name
        self.ceilings: dict[str, float] = {}

    def prepare(self, neg: Negotiation) -> None:
        super().prepare(neg)
        tac = self.tactic
        goal = neg.buyer.get("category_goal", "leverage")
        current = neg.buyer.get("current_unit_price")
        for sid, plan in self.plans.items():
            if plan.open_price is None or plan.target_price is None:
                continue
            if tac.anchor_scale != 1.0:
                base = min(plan.open_price, current) if current else plan.open_price
                target = base * (1 - GOAL_ANCHOR.get(goal, 0.06) * tac.anchor_scale)
                plan.target_price = round(min(max(target, plan.floor_price or 0.0), plan.open_price), 2)
            if tac.budget_share is not None:
                gap = plan.open_price - plan.target_price
                self.ceilings[sid] = round(plan.target_price + tac.budget_share * gap, 2)
            neg.recorder.event(
                "experiment",
                session_id=neg.session_id,
                case_id=neg.case_id,
                supplier_id=sid,
                tactic=tac.name,
                target_price=plan.target_price,
                ceiling=self.ceilings.get(sid),
            )
            log.info("%s %s: target %s ceiling %s", sid, tac.name, plan.target_price, self.ceilings.get(sid))

    def _next_price(self, plan: SupplierPlan, theirs, ours, round_index, their_path=None) -> float:
        price = super()._next_price(plan, theirs, ours, round_index, their_path)
        if self.tactic.conditional and ours and their_path and len(their_path) >= 2:
            if their_path[-1] >= their_path[-2]:
                price = ours[-1]
        ceiling = self.ceilings.get(plan.supplier_id)
        if ceiling is not None:
            price = min(price, max(ceiling, ours[-1] if ours else 0.0))
        return price

    def _opener(self, first: bool) -> str:
        if self.tactic.tone is None:
            return super()._opener(first)
        return TONES[self.tactic.tone][0 if first else 1]

    def _extra_lines(self, neg: Negotiation, plan: SupplierPlan, first: bool) -> list[str]:
        tac, lines = self.tactic, []
        ceiling = self.ceilings.get(plan.supplier_id)
        if ceiling is not None:
            lines.append(
                f"Our management has released a fixed budget for this part: EUR {ceiling:,.2f} per unit on the terms "
                "of option A is the most I am allowed to sign."
                if first
                else f"The budget ceiling of EUR {ceiling:,.2f} per unit on the terms of option A stands; I cannot "
                "sign above it."
            )
        if tac.conditional:
            lines.append(
                "We do not pay more without something in return: each option below gives you something you can use "
                "(commitment, payment or delivery terms) at the price it asks. If you need a higher price, tell us "
                "which term you give for it."
            )
        if tac.questions_per_round:
            start = neg.threads[plan.supplier_id].rounds_used * tac.questions_per_round
            lines += [QUESTIONS[(start + i) % len(QUESTIONS)] for i in range(tac.questions_per_round)]
        if tac.tone and TONES[tac.tone][2]:
            lines.append(TONES[tac.tone][2])
        return lines

That matters more than it sounds: the code freeze and the Live Final are Sunday at 12:00, so the quota starts freeing up only after the final. **The logic of testing follows from that budget:**

1. **Simulator (free, seconds).** Does the code work at all: messages valid, case closes, no crash. It says nothing about score.
2. **Sandbox (free, about 3 minutes).** Does the idea help against real bots? Two demo cases only, so it is a filter: drop what clearly hurts (like `budget` on D02), keep what looks equal or better. Repeat a promising one 2–3 times, because the same strategy can swing by 0.1 between runs.
3. **Practice (10 sessions per run, the scarce resource).** Only strategies that survived the sandbox go here. This is the only place that shows the 10 real case types and the only one that moves the leaderboard. Since only the best score per case counts, a run can't hurt our rank; it only costs quota.
4. **Read the replays of the worst cases.** After a practice run, the arena shows the supplier's reasons per round. That is where the real gains are: we score 0.23–0.31 on P11, P18, P02 and P08, while a tone or anchor tweak moves a case by a few points.
5. **Keep one full practice run for Sunday morning.** The brief asks for a rehearsal of the final setup (all cases in parallel, well inside 8 minutes) before the freeze.
